messages:
alex: heads up — master CI is red after the infra team rolled the compiler image this morning, looks like a bunch of bazel resolve/compile failures on native targets :grimacing:
ci-bot: Build failed: https://ci.redwood.dev/2321 — failing target //core/server:server_lib, error snippet below
jin: here is the top of the log I grabbed:
```
ERROR: /redwood/core/server/BUILD:42:11: Compiling core/server/server.cc failed: cc_wrapper.sh failed: exit 1
server.cc: In function 'void start()':
server.cc:123: undefined reference to `__cxa_thread_atexit_impl'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
maya: that symbol usually shows up with mismatched libstdc++ / GCC versions — which image tag was deployed?
alex: they rolled the gcc-toolchain:2026-03-16 image (sha a1b2c3d) per infra slack. suspect ABI change in stdlibc++
sam: can someone try rerunning the single job first? if it's flaky maybe transient. i kicked a rerun: https://ci.redwood.dev/2321?retry=1
ci-bot: Rerun started by sam — queued on linux-x86-64-builder-3
jin: rerun failed, same link + same undefined ref. Not flaky.
maya: ok assigning a bisect — this smells like a toolchain distro bump. alex / infra, can you pin the old image for the nightly branch while we triage? we should avoid more red commits hitting master. :pray:
alex: temporary pin sounds good. I'll ask infra to pin to gcc-toolchain:2026-03-10 (old sha f4e5d6)
jen: @alex fyi infra is out for lunch but i left a note in infra-channel to roll back the tag for the CI pool — will take ~20m
jin: meanwhile for triage, easiest is to bisect toolchain image commits. maya — want me to run a quick bisect across the recent image builds and test linking?
maya: please do. steps: 1) check out the image repo at infra/images/gcc-toolchain 2) run `scripts/image-bisect --good sha=f4e5d6 --bad sha=a1b2c3d --test cc_binary //core/server:server_lib` 3) report first bad sha
sam: pinging @maya — if the bisect finds a libcxx change we may need to add an explicit link flag as a short-term fix: `-Wl,--no-as-needed -lstdc++` (ugh)
jin: starting the bisect now, will post progress. ETA ~30m depending on image build time
ci-bot: Note: several other targets across repo also show similar link errors, list: //cli:runner, //tools/metrics:collector
maya: thanks, that matches ABI surface area — not isolated to server. alex once infra pins old image can we hold merging for 1 hour? avoid churn while bisecting
alex: will do hold. tagging PRs wip: @eng @product
jin: bisect update: first bad image found at sha 7c9d0ab — this image contains glibc/ld64 bump and a new gcc 12.3.2 build config.
maya: nice find. can someone prepare a minimal reproducer for the infra/images team? jin can you upload the failing linked object and exact link command?
jin: uploaded tarball to https://artifacts.redwood.dev/bisect/2038765432/7c9d0ab.tar.gz and pasted the link in infra channel. includes `ld --version` and link command line used
sam: temporary workaround proposal: revert the image on CI pool to sha f4e5d6 and open a follow-up issue to coordinate a staged rollout with libc++ compatibility tests. I'll open the issue and assign to infra + eng-runtime
maya: agree. also add a perf/regression test that links a few native binaries during image CI so we catch this earlier
alex: thanks team. infra pinned the CI pool to old sha, CI is green again on a quick smoke. i'll leave the hold in place until the staged rollout is ready. :thumbsup:
jin: follow-up: created PR to add a small link-time test and doc for future toolchain upgrades — https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/428
maya: closing loop: created tracking ticket RW-3142 — "toolchain image GCC/ld upgrade caused link-time regressions; add CI link tests + staged rollout" and linked bisect output. assigning to infra + eng-runtime for next steps
alex: great. if anyone wants to add notes to RW-3142 please do. thanks for the quick triage everyone :rocket:
